citation: Zhang M., Jensen K., Sonniks S., Plank B. (2022). SkillSpan: Hard and Soft Skill Extraction from English Job Postings. NAACL, 4962–4984.
finding: Expert annotation of hard and soft skill mentions and domain-adapted extraction models.
limitation: English job postings do not establish performance on Russian/Kazakh texts or AITU profiles.
application: Evaluate extraction separately from ranking; retain reference spans and annotation rules.

citation: Senger E., Zhang M., van der Goot R., Plank B. (2024). Deep Learning-based Computational Job Market Analysis: A Survey on Skill Extraction and Classification from Job Postings. NLP4HR, 1–15.
finding: Survey of terminology, datasets and neural skill extraction methods.
limitation: Different datasets and task definitions prevent direct comparison of reported scores.
application: Define the annotation unit, skill terminology and normalization rules before evaluation.

citation: Zhang M., van der Goot R., Plank B. (2023). ESCOXLM-R: Multilingual Taxonomy-driven Pre-training for the Job Market Domain. ACL, 11871–11890.
finding: Multilingual domain-adaptive pre-training using the ESCO taxonomy.
limitation: Transfer to local occupations and languages requires validation; large-model adaptation needs resources.
application: Maintain canonical skills and aliases; consider ESCO alignment as a future extension.

citation: Nguyen K., Zhang M., Montariol S., Bosselut A. (2024). Rethinking Skill Extraction in the Job Market Domain using Large Language Models. NLP4HR, 27–42.
finding: Few-shot LLM extraction explores complex skill mentions.
limitation: The study does not establish universal superiority over supervised methods; inference requires quality control and resources.
application: Keep external LLM calls optional and assess extraction against fixed labels.

citation: Kavas H., Serra-Vidal M., Wanner L. (2025). Multilingual Skill Extraction for Job Vacancy–Job Seeker Matching in Knowledge Graphs. GenAIK, 146–155.
finding: Multilingual vacancy–candidate matching through skill extraction, ESCO alignment and a knowledge graph.
limitation: The graph pipeline is more complex than a dictionary, and its benefit for AITU graduates remains unmeasured.
application: Compare normalization with semantic expansion and retain the origin of each match.

citation: Laosaengpha N., Tativannarat T., Piansaddhayanon C., Rutherford A., Chuangsuwanich E. (2024). Learning Job Title Representation from Job Description Aggregation Network. Findings of ACL, 1319–1329.
finding: Job-title representations incorporate information from descriptions beyond extracted skills.
limitation: Learning job-title representations is different from assessing an individual candidate.
application: Describe the current score as skill-requirement coverage, not a probability of being hired.

citation: Reimers N., Gurevych I. (2019). Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks. EMNLP-IJCNLP, 3982–3992.
finding: Siamese sentence encoders enable efficient embedding-based text comparison.
limitation: Text similarity does not prove skill proficiency or satisfaction of all job conditions.
application: Use similarity only as supplementary evidence with a limited contribution.

citation: Gao T., Yao X., Chen D. (2021). SimCSE: Simple Contrastive Learning of Sentence Embeddings. EMNLP, 6894–6910.
finding: Contrastive learning produces sentence representations in supervised and unsupervised settings.
limitation: Semantic textual similarity benchmarks do not replace domain-specific matching evaluation.
application: Select an encoder using local ranking quality and latency as well as general benchmarks.

citation: Wang L., Yang N., Huang X., Yang L., Majumder R., Wei F. (2024). Multilingual E5 Text Embeddings: A Technical Report. arXiv:2402.05672.
finding: A family of multilingual retrieval embeddings offers different model sizes.
limitation: Input conventions, model size and inference cost affect suitability.
application: Include E5 in a future comparison; it is not the model currently configured in the prototype.

finding: A standardized vocabulary of occupations and skills.
limitation: A European taxonomy requires validation in the local context.
application: Allow future external identifiers in the skill catalog.

citation: LinkedIn Help. Find how you match up with jobs on LinkedIn.
finding: Profile/resume qualifications are compared with job requirements and explained.
limitation: Availability may depend on subscription and rollout.
application: Compare against modern matching features rather than assuming competitors only list jobs.

citation: Handshake Help Center. Jobs Digests and Recommendations.
finding: Recommendations use student interests and platform activity.
application: Use explicit profile data for the cold-start MVP.

citation: hh.kz. Digitizing candidate skills: guidance on key skills in vacancies.
finding: Key skills are used in job descriptions and search.
limitation: This source does not establish the complete current matching feature set.
application: Use hh.kz as a regional reference; mark unsupported capabilities as not established.

finding: Career roles are linked to skills, courses and practical learning.
limitation: A product description does not establish improved employment outcomes.
application: Distinguish learning recommendations from employment probability.

limitation: Authorization and application-specific checks still require implementation.
application: Use a validated API boundary and generated Swagger documentation.

limitation: Database operation remains a team responsibility.
application: Use foreign keys, uniqueness constraints and migrations.

limitation: A similarity threshold depends on the task and data.
application: Keep the threshold configurable and provide a keyword fallback.
